text: These little thoughts are the rustle of leaves; they have their whisper of joy in my mind.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: I cannot choose the best. The best chooses me.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Rest belongs to the work as the eyelids to the eyes.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The waterfall sings, "I find my song, when I find my freedom."
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The stars are not afraid to appear like fireflies.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Life is given to us, we earn it by giving it.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Never be afraid of the moments—thus sings the voice of the everlasting.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Tiny grass, your steps are small, but you possess the earth under your tread.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: "I give my whole water in joy," sings the waterfall, "though little of it is enough for the thirsty."
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The mist, like love, plays upon the heart of the hills and brings out surprises of beauty.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: He who wants to do good knocks at the gate; he who loves finds the gate open.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The cloud stood humbly in a corner of the sky. The morning crowned it with splendour.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The dust receives insult and in return offers her flowers.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Do not linger to gather flowers to keep them, but walk on, for flowers will keep themselves blooming all your way.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Bees sip honey from flowers and hum their thanks when they leave.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The world has opened its heart of light in the morning. Come out, my heart, with thy love to meet it.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: When we rejoice in our fulness, then we can part with our fruits with joy.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: I have dipped the vessel of my heart into this silent hour; it has filled with love.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: It is the little things that I leave behind for my loved ones—great things are for everyone.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The sunshine greets me with a smile. The rain, his sad sister, talks to my heart.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Sit still my heart, do not raise your dust. Let the world find its way to you.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Night's darkness is a bag that bursts with the gold of the dawn.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Men are cruel, but Man is kind.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Life has become richer by the love that has been lost.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Let him only see the thorns who has eyes to see the rose.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Wayside grass, love the star, then your dreams will come out in flowers.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: I came to your shore as a stranger, I lived in your house as a guest, I leave your door as a friend, my earth.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: We live in this world when we love it.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Love is life in its fulness like the cup with its wine.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: The storm of the last night has crowned this morning with golden peace.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Thy sunshine smiles upon the winter days of my heart, never doubting of its spring flowers.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: While I enjoy the friendship of the seasons I trust that nothing can make life a burden to me.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: The year beginning with younger hope than ever!
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: There is nothing like this serenity, this comfort, this peace, this deep contentment, to be found anywhere on land.
author: Mark Twain

text: I must learn how to be cheerful and happy.
author: Oscar Wilde

text: To hope the best is pious, brave, and wise, and may itself procure what it presumes.
author: Edward Young

text: Ask thought for joy; grow rich, and hoard within.
author: Edward Young

text: Up! up! my friend, and quit your books, or surely you'll grow double.
author: William Wordsworth

text: The simple flowers of our Spring are what I want to see again.
author: John Keats
